title: Cab directs every solo: the high F lesson on "Geechee Joe"
summary: At a morning Strand Theater show Jones skipped his usual high F ending and Cab, who directs each soloist's ending with his stick, scolded him; he says late nights are no excuse.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: you know, and he's just hollering for more. Stuff's hollering for more. And over there you played just what you were supposed to play, you know, with Cab. So I said, well, that's it. I'm not going to kill myself with the whiskey over there with Stuff, drinking every night, you know. And had had a couple of attacks then. So I was able to come out of it. So I -- this is going to be it. So one morning (Unintelligible). We're on the Strand Theater, and he comes out in his zoot suit and his chain, and he walks around, and we make an introduction and go into I think two choruses of the blues in E-flat. And at the end of it I'd always end up on F, high F, you know. And I didn't know that he was directing my solo until one day I'd been fooling around all night, you know. Instead of going to half hour, about 10:30 in the morning, at the Strand Theater. And I didn't feel like making no F there that morning. So I played something else, you know. And when I got ready to end up I just ended up maybe (Singing), something like that, and so he called me after the finale, you know, and he said, "You messed me up this morning." And I said, "How?" He said, "Well, you always made that F up there on Geechee Joe'." I said, "Oh, yeah." And he said, "Well, you didn't make it this morning." I said, "No, I didn't feel like making it this morning because I was fooling around out there all night, you know, and I wasn't together. I didn't get to warm up good." He said, "Yeah, but don't do that, because you can't see me, but

when you're playing I'm directing all your notes." And he said, "I direct all that stuff right pointing to you, and you're supposed to go up on that F and I threw my stick up, and I threw my stick up this morning and you made something else down here." So these are the little things in life, you know, that you learn as you go along, you know. Now, it tells you from now on don't be so smart, trying to end up on F, you know, unless you intend to do it all the time, under any conditions.

Under any condition. I don't care if you've been up all night and you've had no sleep, don't. I don't want to hear that, uh-uh. Because he'd tell you in a minute, you know. And he was right if you look into it. You go out and hang out with him. Sometimes he'd take Tyree or me or somebody to go along with him, and you're hanging out, you know, and up all night and fooling around, and then you get in bed and maybe get a couple of hours sleep, and then you might do this on a stage, you know, on a big stage, it looks bad, you know, in the Chicago Theater or something.

And he catches you. "Oh, no, wake up there. Don't do that. Don't do that." So Tyree say, "I was with you." He said, "Look, Thatain't had nothing to do with it. Today is another day. Play my music now." Which is right.
